title: Esports Championship Week: MOUZ Sweeps Beijing, KRÜ Blaze Makes Latin American History, and the Worlds Final Is Set for Saturday
excerpt: MOUZ won IEM Beijing without dropping a map, KRÜ Blaze became the first Latin American team to win the women's Valorant world title, and Gen.G meets Bilibili Gaming in the League of Legends Worlds final Saturday in Brooklyn.
content:
Three champions, three stages: esports heads into a championship week with titles decided in Beijing and São Paulo — and the biggest one of all, the League of Legends World Championship, still to be played Saturday in Brooklyn.

In Counter-Strike 2, MOUZ beat The MongolZ 3-0 in the IEM Beijing 2026 grand final on Sunday, Nov. 8 — Mirage 13-5, Dust2 13-6, Inferno 13-4 — and did not drop a single map all tournament, winning all six group-stage maps as well. It was the organization’s first-ever IEM title and the first IEM in Beijing since 2019. MOUZ collected $360,000 of the $1,250,000 prize pool, and in-game leader Dorian “xertioN” Berman was named MVP — the first MVP award of his career — with a 1.44 rating in the final. Natus Vincere took third, beating BetBoom 2-0.

The CS2 scene has already moved on. BLAST Rivals opened today in Hong Kong, and G2 Esports stunned world No. 1 MOUZ 2-1 on opening day — MOUZ took Nuke 13-7 before G2 won Ancient 16-14 in overtime and Inferno 13-7. Team Spirit survived a 13-0 whitewash on Nuke by FUT Esports before winning its series 2-1. FURIA, Vitality, Spirit and G2 all clinched playoff spots on day one, with the grand final set for Sunday, Nov. 15.

In Valorant, KRÜ Blaze of Argentina and Latin America beat Gentle Mates GC 3-2 in a five-map grand final on Nov. 1 at Riot Games Arena in São Paulo, taking the decider on Ascent 13-8 to win the Game Changers Championship — the women’s world title. KRÜ Blaze is the first Latin American team to win the title and the first ever to win it from the lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run. KRÜ took $180,000 from a $500,000 prize pool; Gentle Mates earned $100,000 as runners-up, and Amaro “tok1o” Miranda was named MVP with 84 kills across the five maps. It was the last standalone Game Changers Championship: starting in 2027, the event will be held alongside VALORANT Champions in Austin, Texas, Sept. 16-Oct. 10, 2027.

In League of Legends, the Worlds 2026 final is set for Saturday, Nov. 14, at 2 p.m. ET at Barclays Center in Brooklyn — Gen.G vs. Bilibili Gaming. Gen.G swept LYON 3-0 in the quarterfinal and Invictus Gaming 3-0 in the semifinal on Nov. 7 in Allen, Texas, reaching its first Worlds final since winning as Samsung Galaxy in 2017, and star mid laner Chovy’s first Worlds final in his eighth appearance. Bilibili Gaming ended defending champion T1’s run of three straight world titles with a 3-1 semifinal win on Nov. 8, after sweeping Dplus KIA 3-0 in the quarterfinal. BLG has never won Worlds; its best finish was runner-up in 2024, losing 3-2 to T1.

Next on the CS2 calendar: the PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs Nov. 24-Dec. 13, with 32 teams and a $1,250,000 prize pool, and playoffs at Singapore Indoor Stadium.

Sources: LoLNow, updated Nov. 10, 2026; TalkEsport, Nov. 8-9, 2026; KeenGamer, Nov. 9-10, 2026; Dot Esports, Nov. 3, 2026; Esports Insider, Nov. 3-4, 2026; SportsBriefly, Nov. 11, 2026; ESTNN, Nov. 5, 2026.
